Current operational status of the loyalty program: active (accepting enrollments and transactions), inactive (not operational), suspended (temporarily paused), pilot (testing phase), or sunset (being phased out).

Annual membership fee charged to maintain this tier status, if applicable. Null or zero indicates no fee. Used for premium tier monetization.

Indicates whether members in this tier receive a special birthday reward (e.g., free item, bonus points, discount). True if eligible, false otherwise.
Short alphanumeric code uniquely identifying the tier (e.g., BRONZE, SILVER, GOLD, PLATINUM). Used as business identifier in operational systems and reporting.

Date when this tier configuration was retired or replaced. Null indicates the tier is currently active. Used for tier lifecycle management and historical analysis.

Number of days after tier expiration during which members retain tier benefits before downgrade. Used to provide buffer period for re-qualification.
URL path to the tier badge or icon image asset used in member portal, mobile app, and digital communications. Supports tier visual identity and gamification.
Timestamp when this tier record was last updated. Used for audit trail, change tracking, and data synchronization.
Date when this tier was officially launched to the market and communicated to guests. May differ from effective_start_date for soft launches or pilot programs.
Maximum percentage discount that can be applied when redeeming points for rewards in this tier (e.g., 20.00 for 20% max discount). Used to control reward economics and prevent abuse.
Username or identifier of the user who last modified this tier configuration. Used for audit trail and accountability.
Human-readable display name of the loyalty tier (e.g., Bronze Member, Silver Member, Gold Member, Platinum Elite). Used in guest-facing communications and marketing materials.
Multiplier applied to base points accrual for members in this tier (e.g., 1.0 for base, 1.5 for 50% bonus, 2.0 for double points). Used to calculate accelerated points earning.
Indicates whether members in this tier receive priority customer support (e.g., dedicated phone line, faster response times). True if eligible, false otherwise.
The metric used to determine tier qualification (points accrued, visit count, total spend amount, or transaction count). Defines how qualification_threshold is interpreted.
Number of days over which the qualification threshold must be met (e.g., 365 for annual qualification, 90 for quarterly). Null indicates lifetime accumulation.
Numeric threshold value required to qualify for this tier (e.g., 1000 points, 25 visits, $500 spend). Interpretation depends on qualification_metric.
Bonus points awarded to members in this tier for each successful referral of a new loyalty program member. Used to incentivize member acquisition through word-of-mouth.
Indicates whether unused points can roll over to the next qualification period for members in this tier. True if rollover is allowed, false if points expire at period end.

Integer defining the hierarchical display order of tiers (e.g., 1 for Bronze, 2 for Silver, 3 for Gold, 4 for Platinum). Lower values represent entry-level tiers; higher values represent premium tiers.

Description of the target guest segment this tier is designed to attract and retain (e.g., frequent visitors, high spenders, digital-first guests, family diners). Used for marketing strategy and program design.

Current lifecycle status of the tier. Active tiers are available for member assignment; inactive tiers are temporarily disabled; retired tiers are no longer offered but may have legacy members; pending tiers are configured but not yet launched.
Indicates whether members should receive automated notification when they qualify for upgrade to this tier. True if notification is enabled, false otherwise.
Number of days a member retains this tier status after qualification before re-evaluation (e.g., 365 for annual renewal). Null indicates permanent tier assignment.
One-time bonus points awarded to a member upon first achieving this tier. Used to incentivize tier progression and enhance member engagement.

Foreign key linking to loyalty.program. Business justification: Links offers to the franchisee that runs them, required for franchise‑specific marketing ROI analysis.
Username or user ID of the marketing manager who approved the offer for distribution. Null if offer is still in draft status.
Timestamp when the offer was approved for distribution. Null if offer is still in draft status.
Indicates whether the offer is automatically applied at checkout when eligibility criteria are met (True) or requires manual code entry by the member (False).
Number of bonus loyalty points awarded when the offer is redeemed. Applicable to bonus_points and challenge offer types. Null for other offer types.

Comma-separated list of days of the week when the offer is valid (e.g., monday,tuesday,wednesday). Null if valid all days.

Detailed marketing copy describing the offer terms, benefits, and redemption instructions displayed to members.
Mechanism of discount for discount-type offers: percentage (e.g., 20% off), fixed_amount (e.g., $5 off), free_item (specific SKU at no charge). Null for non-discount offer types.
Numeric value of the discount: percentage (e.g., 20.00 for 20%), dollar amount (e.g., 5.00 for $5 off), or 0 for free_item offers. Null for non-discount offer types.

Date when the offer expires and is no longer redeemable. Null for evergreen offers without a fixed expiration.
Estimated financial cost to the business for each redemption of this offer, including discount value and incremental COGS. Used for campaign budget planning and ROI analysis.

URL to the promotional image or banner displayed with the offer in mobile app, email, and digital channels.
Minimum transaction subtotal (before tax) required to qualify for the offer. Null if no minimum purchase requirement.
Minimum number of visits in the trailing 90 days required for a member to be eligible for this offer. Null if no visit frequency requirement.
Timestamp when the offer record was last modified in the Salesforce CRM system.
Marketing name of the offer displayed to loyalty members in app, email, and push notifications.

Current lifecycle state of the offer: draft (being designed), scheduled (approved, awaiting start date), active (live and redeemable), paused (temporarily suspended), expired (end date passed), cancelled (terminated before expiration).

Classification of the offer mechanism: discount (percentage or dollar off), bonus_points (accelerated points accrual), free_item (complimentary menu item), bogo (buy-one-get-one), challenge (gamification task), sweepstakes (prize drawing entry).
Indicates whether this offer is personalized to individual members based on purchase history and preferences (True) or is a mass offer distributed to all eligible members (False).
Multiplier applied to base points accrual during the offer period (e.g., 2.00 for double points, 3.00 for triple points). Applicable to bonus_points offers. Null for other offer types.
Display priority ranking for this offer when multiple offers are available to a member. Lower numbers indicate higher priority (1 = highest).
Channel(s) where the offer can be redeemed: pos (in-store point of sale), olo (online ordering), mobile_app, kiosk, drive_thru, all_channels (omnichannel).
Current cumulative count of redemptions for this offer across all members. Updated in near-real-time from POS and OLO transaction feeds.
Maximum number of times a single loyalty member can redeem this offer during its active period. Null for unlimited redemptions.
Indicates whether this offer can be combined with other offers in a single transaction. True = stackable, False = exclusive.
Date when the offer becomes active and available for redemption by eligible members.
Marketing team's target goal for total number of redemptions during the offer period. Used for campaign performance evaluation.
Legal terms and conditions governing the offer, including eligibility, restrictions, expiration, and disclaimers. Required for compliance with FTC advertising regulations.
Maximum total number of redemptions allowed across all members for this offer (budget cap). Null for unlimited total redemptions.
Unique identifier for each points transaction record in the loyalty ledger. Serves as the immutable primary key for this financial-grade system of record.

Foreign key linking to loyalty.accrual_rule. Business justification: Each points accrual entry in the ledger is generated by a specific accrual rule (e.g., base earn rate, bonus multiplier rule, birthday bonus rule). Linking points_ledger.accrual_rule_id → loyalty.accr
Unique identifier of the loyalty program member whose points balance is affected by this transaction. Links to the member master record.

Foreign key linking to loyalty.offer. Business justification: Bonus points accruals in the ledger are frequently tied to specific promotional offers (e.g., double points weekend, birthday bonus offer, new member enrollment offer). Linking points_ledger.offer_id

Identifier of the system user or customer service agent who authorized and executed the manual adjustment or reversal. Populated for adjust and reversal transactions. Critical for SOX compliance and fraud prevention.

Reference to the originating order transaction that triggered this points movement. Populated for earn and redeem transactions tied to guest purchases. Null for non-order events such as bonus awards, expirations, or manual adjustments.

Identifier of the restaurant location where this points transaction originated. Populated for POS and kiosk transactions. Null for OLO, mobile app, or admin transactions not tied to a specific physical location.

Identifier of the franchise entity that owns or operates the restaurant where this transaction occurred. Used for royalty calculations and franchise performance analytics. Null for company-owned locations or non-location transactions.

Reference to the original points_ledger_id that this reversal transaction is canceling. Populated only for reversal transaction types. Creates an audit chain linking reversals to their source transactions.

Identifier of the specific reward item redeemed by the member. Populated only for redeem transaction types. Links to the rewards catalog to identify what was claimed (free item, discount, experience).

The unique transaction identifier from the originating source system. Enables end-to-end traceability and reconciliation between the loyalty ledger and upstream systems. Format varies by source system.
Identifier of the loyalty membership tier the member held at the time of this transaction. Used to determine earn rates, bonus multipliers, and redemption privileges. Links to tier master data.
Standardized code explaining why a manual adjustment or reversal was made. Populated only for adjust and reversal transaction types. Supports audit compliance and customer service quality tracking.

Free-text explanation provided by the customer service representative or system administrator who initiated the adjustment. Populated for adjust and reversal transactions. Supports audit trail and dispute resolution.

Identifier of the processing batch or job that created this ledger entry. Used for bulk operations such as nightly expiration runs, mass bonus awards, or system migrations. Null for real-time individual transactions.
The fiscal period (month or accounting period number) within the fiscal year when this transaction occurred. Supports monthly financial close, P&L reporting, and loyalty liability accrual tracking.

The fiscal year in which this points transaction occurred, derived from transaction_timestamp. Supports financial reporting, GAAP revenue recognition for breakage, and year-over-year loyalty program analytics.

Flag indicating whether this transaction has been voided or reversed by a subsequent transaction. True if a reversal exists, false otherwise. Immutable ledger entries are never deleted, only marked as voided.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the order total amount. Supports multi-currency loyalty programs for international operations. Null for non-order transactions.

The total monetary value of the order that triggered this points transaction, in the local currency. Used to calculate points earn rate and for financial reconciliation. Null for non-order transactions.

The cumulative running balance of points for this member immediately after this transaction was applied. Provides audit trail and reconciliation capability. Must equal prior balance plus points_delta.

The signed integer change in points balance for this transaction. Positive values represent accruals (earn, bonus), negative values represent deductions (redeem, expire, adjust downward). Zero-delta entries are not permitted.

The rate at which points were earned per currency unit spent. Example: 1.0000 means 1 point per dollar, 2.0000 means 2 points per dollar (double points promotion). Populated for earn transactions, null otherwise.

The date on which the points earned in this transaction will expire if not redeemed. Populated only for earn and bonus transaction types. Null for redeem, expire, and adjust transactions. Supports FIFO expiration logic and member communication.

The date and time when this ledger entry was committed to the loyalty system of record. May differ from transaction_timestamp for batch processing or delayed reconciliation. Used for ETL audit and SLA monitoring.
Human-readable store or unit number for the restaurant location. Denormalized for operational reporting and guest service. Null for non-location-specific transactions.

The originating channel or interface through which this points transaction was initiated: POS (Point of Sale in-store), OLO (Online Ordering web platform), mobile_app (native mobile application), kiosk (self-service in-store kiosk), 3PD (Third-Party Delivery partner), call_center (phone order), admin (manual back-office adjustment). [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: pos|olo|mobile_app|kiosk|3pd|call_center|admin — 7 candidates stripped; promote to reference product]
Human-readable order number or receipt identifier from the POS or OLO system. Provides guest-facing reference for customer service inquiries. Null for non-order transactions.

Code identifying the operational system that originated this points transaction. Supports multi-system integration and data lineage tracking. Examples: micros_pos (Oracle MICROS POS), olo_platform (Olo Digital Ordering), salesforce_crm (Salesforce Marketing Cloud), loyalty_engine (core loyalty platform), admin_portal (back-office admin tool).
The precise date and time when this points transaction occurred in the source system. Represents the business event time, not the ETL load time. Critical for sequencing and audit.

Classification of the points movement: earn (points accrued from purchase or activity), redeem (points spent on rewards), expire (points lapsed due to inactivity or time limit), adjust (manual correction by support or system), bonus (promotional award), reversal (cancellation of prior transaction).
The date and time when this transaction was voided by a reversal. Null if the transaction has not been voided. Supports audit trail and reconciliation.

Reference to the restaurant unit where the redemption occurred.
Reference to the restaurant unit where the redemption occurred.
Reference to the specific reward item redeemed from the loyalty rewards catalog.

Timestamp when this redemption record was first created in the loyalty system.
Three-letter ISO 4217 currency code for the discount amount (e.g., USD, EUR, GBP).
The time-of-day segment when the redemption occurred, used for analyzing redemption patterns by service period.
Monetary discount value applied to the order as a result of the reward redemption, in local currency.
Date on which the redeemed reward was set to expire if not used, relevant for tracking near-expiry redemption behavior.
Boolean indicator set to true if the redemption was flagged for potential fraudulent activity or policy violation.
Numeric fraud risk score assigned by the loyalty platform fraud detection engine, ranging from 0.00 (low risk) to 100.00 (high risk).
Alphanumeric confirmation code generated upon successful fulfillment of the redemption, used for audit and reconciliation.
Loyalty program membership tier of the member at the time of redemption, used for tier-based redemption analysis.
Free-text notes or comments captured by the employee or system regarding special circumstances or issues with the redemption.
Total order amount after the loyalty reward discount was applied, representing the net revenue from the transaction.
Total order amount before the loyalty reward discount was applied, used for calculating incremental ACV (Average Check Value) impact.
Loyalty points balance of the member immediately after this redemption transaction.
Loyalty points balance of the member immediately before this redemption transaction.
Number of loyalty points deducted from the member account to redeem this reward.
Externally visible unique business identifier for the redemption transaction, used for customer service and tracking.

Current lifecycle status of the redemption transaction. Date and time when the loyalty member initiated the reward redemption at the point of sale or online ordering platform.
Free-text explanation for why the redemption was reversed or voided, captured for customer service and fraud analysis.
Date and time when the redemption was reversed or voided, if applicable.

Classification of the reward redeemed. Discount for percentage or fixed amount off, free item for complimentary menu item, BOGO (Buy One Get One) for promotional offer, upgrade for size or quality enhancement, combo deal for bundled offer, birthday reward for member birthday incentive.

Indicates how the redemption was initiated. Manual for member-selected reward, automatic for system-applied offer, promotional trigger for campaign-driven redemption, gamification for achievement-based reward, tier benefit for membership tier perk.
Name of the third-party delivery platform if the redemption occurred through a 3PD channel (e.g., DoorDash, Uber Eats, Grubhub).
Timestamp when this redemption record was last modified in the loyalty system.

description: Rank of the menu item within its menu category at the restaurant for the reporting period, ordered by units sold descending. Used to identify top and bottom performers within each category for menu rationalization decisions.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — PMIX Category Ranking; NRA Menu Engineering Standards

description: Total Cost of Goods Sold (COGS) for the menu item during the reporting period, calculated as units sold multiplied by the item's standard recipe cost. Core input for menu engineering profitability analysis.
reference: SAP S/4HANA — CO Cost Accounting; MarketMan Inventory Management — Recipe Costing; GAAP/IFRS

description: Cost of Goods Sold as a percentage of net sales (CoGS%) for the menu item during the reporting period. A key menu engineering metric used to classify items and assess profitability relative to category benchmarks.
reference: SAP S/4HANA — CO Profitability Analysis; NRA Menu Engineering Standards; GAAP/IFRS

description: Total monetary value of complimentary (comped) menu items given during the reporting period. Represents a direct cost to the restaurant and is tracked for P&L accuracy and loss prevention.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Comp Tracking; SAP S/4HANA — Cost Accounting; GAAP/IFRS

description: Number of complimentary (comped) units of this menu item given to guests during the reporting period (e.g., for service recovery, employee meals, or promotional giveaways). Tracked for cost control and loss prevention.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Comp Tracking; NRA Operational Standards

description: Contribution margin for the menu item during the reporting period, calculated as net sales minus COGS. Represents the dollar contribution of the item toward covering fixed costs and generating profit. Core metric in menu engineering star/plow-horse/puzzle/dog classification.
reference: SAP S/4HANA — CO Contribution Margin Analysis; NRA Menu Engineering Standards; GAAP/IFRS

description: Timestamp when this PMIX record was first created in the Silver layer data product. Supports audit trail, data lineage, and SLA monitoring for data pipeline freshness.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; GAAP/IFRS Audit Trail Requirements

description: ISO 4217 three-letter currency code for all monetary amounts in this PMIX record (e.g., USD, CAD, GBP). Supports multi-currency reporting for international restaurant operations.
reference: ISO 4217 Currency Codes; SAP S/4HANA — Currency Configuration; GAAP/IFRS

description: Daypart segment during which the menu item sales are recorded (e.g., breakfast, lunch, dinner). Daypart is a core foodservice industry segmentation concept used for menu engineering, labor scheduling, and promotional analysis.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Daypart Configuration; NRA Daypart Standards

description: Total value of discounts, promotional reductions, and coupon redemptions applied to the menu item during the reporting period. Used to reconcile gross to net sales and evaluate promotional effectiveness.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Discount Tracking; SAP S/4HANA — Revenue Deductions; GAAP/IFRS

description: Total gross sales revenue generated by the menu item during the reporting period, before discounts, voids, and comps. Expressed in local currency. Core component of the MONETARY_TRIPLET for revenue reporting.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Sales Summary; SAP S/4HANA — Revenue Accounting; GAAP/IFRS Revenue Recognition

description: Indicates whether the menu item was available for sale during the entire reporting period at the restaurant. A value of False may indicate a stock-out, 86'd item, or temporary removal from the menu, which can suppress PMIX figures.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Item Availability; MarketMan Inventory Management — Stock Status

description: Indicates whether the menu item is a Limited Time Offer (LTO) during the reporting period. LTO items require separate PMIX tracking to evaluate promotional performance and inform future LTO decisions.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Menu Item Attributes; NRA Menu Engineering Standards

description: The menu category to which the item belongs (e.g., Burgers, Beverages, Sides, Desserts, LTO). Used for category-level PMIX analysis and menu engineering decisions. [ENUM-REF-CANDIDATE: entree|beverage|side|dessert|appetizer|lto|combo|condiment — promote to reference product]
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Menu Category Master; NRA Menu Engineering Standards

description: Menu engineering quadrant classification of the item for the reporting period based on the Boston Consulting Group (BCG) matrix adapted for foodservice: Star (high popularity, high margin), Plow Horse (high popularity, low margin), Puzzle (low popularity, high margin), Dog (low popularity, low margin). Core output of menu engineering analysis.
reference: NRA Menu Engineering Standards; Kasavana & Smith Menu Engineering Methodology

description: The standard listed menu price for the item at the restaurant during the reporting period. Used to calculate price realization (average selling price vs. list price) and assess discount impact.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Menu Price Configuration; FDA Menu Labeling Requirements

description: The percentage of total units sold at the restaurant during the reporting period that this menu item represents. Core Product Mix (PMIX) metric used to identify high-velocity and low-velocity items for menu engineering decisions.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — PMIX Report; NRA Menu Engineering Standards

description: Net sales revenue for the menu item after deducting discounts, voids, and comps from gross sales. The primary revenue figure used in P&L reporting, PMIX analysis, and AUV calculations.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Net Sales; SAP S/4HANA — Net Revenue; GAAP/IFRS Revenue Recognition

description: Rank of the menu item across all menu items at the restaurant for the reporting period, ordered by units sold descending. Provides a holistic view of item velocity for menu engineering and operational prioritization.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — PMIX Overall Ranking; NRA Menu Engineering Standards

description: Indicates whether the restaurant is company-owned or franchised. Enables separate PMIX benchmarking and menu engineering analysis across ownership models, which is critical for franchise royalty and P&L reporting.
reference: FranConnect — Franchise Classification; FTC Franchise Disclosure Regulations; IFA Standards

description: Lifecycle status of this PMIX record in the Silver layer. 'active' indicates the current valid record; 'revised' indicates the record has been superseded by a correction; 'voided' indicates the record was invalidated due to a data quality issue.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; GAAP/IFRS Audit Trail Requirements

description: Total monetary value of refunds issued for this menu item during the reporting period. Used in net revenue reconciliation and guest satisfaction analysis.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Refund Tracking; SAP S/4HANA — Revenue Adjustments; GAAP/IFRS

description: Number of refunds issued for this menu item during the reporting period. Elevated refund counts may indicate quality issues, order accuracy problems, or guest dissatisfaction.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Refund Tracking; PCI DSS — Refund Transaction Controls

description: Calendar date for which this PMIX record applies. Used for daily and weekly menu engineering analysis and comparable store sales (Comp Sales / SSS) reporting.
reference: NRA Industry Reporting Standards; GAAP/IFRS Fiscal Period Alignment

description: Granularity of the PMIX record — whether it represents a daily, weekly, or daypart-level aggregation. Determines how units sold and revenue figures should be interpreted.
The restaurant service format (Quick-Service Restaurant (QSR), casual, or fine-dining) associated with this PMIX record. Supports cross-format menu performance benchmarking.
reference: FranConnect — Restaurant Format Classification; NRA Industry Standards

description: The percentage of total net sales revenue at the restaurant during the reporting period attributable to this menu item. Distinct from menu mix percentage (unit-based); this is revenue-based mix used for revenue contribution analysis.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Revenue Mix Report; SAP S/4HANA — Revenue Analysis; NRA Standards

description: The Stock Keeping Unit (SKU) code assigned to the menu item in the POS and inventory management systems. Used to reconcile PMIX data with supply chain and inventory records in MarketMan.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Item SKU; MarketMan Inventory Management — SKU Master

description: Total number of hours during the reporting period that the menu item was unavailable for sale (e.g., due to stock-out or being 86'd). Used to adjust PMIX velocity calculations and identify supply chain or inventory issues.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Item 86 Tracking; MarketMan Inventory Management

description: Total number of individual menu item units sold during the reporting period at the restaurant. The primary volume metric in PMIX analysis and menu engineering.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Sales Transaction Data; NRA PMIX Reporting Standards

description: Timestamp when this PMIX record was last modified in the Silver layer, such as when a correction or revision was applied. Supports audit trail and change tracking for data governance.
reference: Internal Data Governance Standard; GAAP/IFRS Audit Trail Requirements

description: Total monetary value of voided transactions for this menu item during the reporting period. Used alongside void count for loss prevention analysis and operational quality monitoring.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Void Tracking; SAP S/4HANA — Revenue Adjustments

description: Number of voided transactions for this menu item during the reporting period. Voids indicate order errors, customer changes, or operational issues and are tracked separately from discounts for loss prevention and operational quality analysis.
reference: Oracle MICROS POS — Void Tracking; NRA Operational Standards
